messages.subject: Why does the wilcox test produce a result if the code is miswritten instead of an error
messages.subject_clean: Why does the wilcox test produce a result if the code is miswritten instead of an error
messages.body_plain:
Why does the wilcoxon (aka, the Mann-Whitney U test) produce a result when the code is written like this:

1> wilcox.test(sz251$age_first_bili, sz251$phototherapy)

	Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  sz251$age_first_bili and sz251$phototherapy

W = 63001, p-value < 2.2e-16

alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

It should be written like this:

2> wilcox.test(age_first_bili ~ phototherapy, data =sz251 )

	Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  age_first_bili by phototherapy

W = 4062, p-value = 0.6286

alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

This (2)  is the correct output. Why doesn’t 1 print an error?!!

>From jamovi:
